title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 73 (Prohibition on acceptance of deposits from public)

content.overview: Section 73 prohibits acceptance of deposits from the public except as the Chapter allows, and tightly conditions acceptance from members.
content.glance: Section 73 prohibits acceptance of deposits from the public except as the Chapter allows, and tightly conditions acceptance from members.
content.study: Deposit is defined in s. 2(31) and excludes prescribed categories such as amounts from banks and specified institutions. Under s. 73 a company may accept deposits from members only if authorised by a resolution, after issuing a circular, filing it with the Registrar, providing deposit insurance as prescribed or the applicable exemption, and creating a deposit repayment reserve of at least 20 per cent of deposits maturing in the following financial year, to be kept in a scheduled bank. Credit rating and security conditions apply where prescribed. The company must certify that it has not defaulted in repayment of deposits or interest. Public deposits are not allowed under s. 73; eligible public companies use s. 76. Amounts remaining unpaid can be treated as unsecured and rank with other unsecured debt on winding up.

distinctions: Section 73 is member deposits and the public prohibition. Section 76 is public deposits by eligible companies. Section 74 deals with pre-Act deposits.

questionsAndAnswers.question: May every company invite deposits from the public under s. 73?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. Section 73 prohibits public invitation. Public deposits require s. 76 eligibility.
